chapter: Theaters, the Navy and the Singletons' partnership
title: Sleigh bells bought at Connie's Inn in 1929
summary: The sleigh bells in the case were bought in 1929 for a Christmas show at Connie's Inn, when Hal Baquet played Santa Claus. Dance remarks on percussion fashions today.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: Those bells now, what did you use them for? I've got them over there in the case, those bells that you had?
Well that was for a Christmas show in Connie's Inn. You see I bought that when I was in Connie's Inn.
You still use them. He uses them during the holidays.

For Christmas, Santa, Hal Bacquet (Falcon) was Santa Claus I believe. Big guy, he sure didn't look like Santa Claus. And every now and then Hal would have me come in with the sleigh bells. (SOUND OF BELLS IN BACKGROUND). Well, I bought them in 1929.

Well you know something, you're just about in the fashion now because that's all they're doing. If you went to see Herbie Wein's Hancock's band at the George (Wingate) festival. Now these people play saxophones and flutes and everything. But half the time they are standing up just jingling bells. You know, it's really getting kind of funny. There is nothing going on except people jingling and playing percussion.
